ai.literal: Excellence of tongue called possession of goodness, that goodness in any goodness included even is not.
ai.translation: The possession of goodness called excellence of speech is a unique wealth. That goodness is not included in any other kind of goodness.
ai.modern: நாவன்மை என்று சொல்லப்படும் நற்பண்பு ஒரு தனிப்பட்ட செல்வமாகும். அந்தச் செல்வம் வேறு எந்தச் செல்வங்களுக்குள்ளும் அடங்குவது அன்று.
ai.explanation: The poet defines the power of speech as a unique and unparalleled wealth. By stating that the 'excellence of the tongue' (நாநலம்) is not included in any other kind of goodness, the couplet emphasizes its distinct nature. It implies that eloquence is an independent asset that cannot be replaced by other forms of wealth or virtue.

ai.literal: Prosperity and ruin by it because of arising, having guarded, ward off slip in speech.
ai.translation: Since both prosperity and ruin arise from it, carefully guard against any slip in your speech.
ai.modern: ஆக்கமும் அழிவும் ஒருவருடைய சொல்லாலேயே வருவதால், பேசும் சொல்லில் பிழை ஏற்படாமல் விழிப்புடன் காக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the profound impact of one's words. The words 'ākkam' (prosperity or constructive good) and 'kēṭu' (ruin or destructive evil) show that speech has the power to build up or tear down a person's life. Because such significant outcomes arise directly from speech, the speaker is advised to be extremely vigilant. The phrase 'kāttu ōmpal' (guard and protect) stresses the active, continuous effort required to prevent any 'cōrvu' (slip, error, or careless mistake) in what is said.

words.gloss: even those who did not listen

ai.literal: Those who listened captivating having the nature, even those who did not listen to desire speaking is speech.
ai.translation: True speech has the quality to captivate those who listen, and to make even those who have not listened desire to hear it.
ai.modern: கேட்டவர்களைத் தன்வயப்படுத்தும் தன்மையுடையதாகவும், கேட்காதவர்களும் கேட்க விரும்புமாறு பேசுவதே சிறந்த சொல்லாற்றல் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true power of speech. It states that effective speech must have two qualities. First, it must captivate and hold the attention of those who are already listening. Second, its reputation and appeal must be so strong that even those who have not yet heard it desire to listen. The word 'பிணிக்கும்' (binding) vividly describes how a good speaker holds the audience spellbound.

ai.literal: Capacity having known let one speak the word; virtue and wealth than that greater is not.
ai.translation: Speak your words after understanding the capacity of your listeners. There is no virtue or wealth greater than that.
ai.modern: கேட்போரின் தன்மையை அறிந்து சொற்களைச் சொல்ல வேண்டும். அதைவிடச் சிறந்த அறமும் பொருளும் வேறு இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet advises speakers to carefully assess the capacity ('திறன்') of their audience before speaking. When words are chosen to perfectly match the listeners' understanding, communication becomes highly effective. The poet emphasizes the value of this skill by stating that there is no greater source of virtue ('அறன்') or wealth ('பொருள்') than such well-judged speech.

ai.literal: Speak a word, having known the absence of another word defeating that word.
ai.translation: Speak a word only after making sure that no other word can defeat it.
ai.modern: நீங்கள் சொல்லும் சொல்லை வெல்லக்கூடிய வேறு ஒரு சொல் இல்லை என்பதை உறுதியாக அறிந்த பிறகே அச்சொல்லைச் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of choosing invincible words when speaking. A speaker must carefully evaluate their arguments before uttering them. They should only speak a word after ensuring that no counter-argument or alternative word can defeat it. This highlights the power of precise, unassailable speech in effective communication.

ai.literal: So as to please, themselves having spoken; others' speech essence grasping; of excellence flaw those without, principle.
ai.translation: Speaking so as to please their listeners and grasping the essence of what others say is the principle of the flawlessly excellent.
ai.modern: கேட்பவர் விரும்பும்படி இனிமையாகப் பேசி, மற்றவர் சொல்லும் கருத்துக்களின் பயனைத் தான் உணர்ந்து கொள்வது மாண்பில் குற்றமற்றவர்களின் இயல்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ideal communication style of truly excellent people. First, they speak in a way that pleases and engages their listeners. Second, when others speak, they look past any superficial flaws to grasp the true essence and benefit of the message. Such balanced mastery of both speaking and listening is the guiding principle of those who are flawlessly great.

ai.literal: Speaking capable-man, slip without-he, fears-not-he, him, conflict conquering, for anyone, difficult.
ai.translation: It is difficult for anyone to defeat in a conflict a man who is capable in speech, who makes no slips, and who knows no fear.
ai.modern: பேசுவதில் வல்லவனாகவும், சோர்வு இல்லாதவனாகவும், யாருக்கும் அஞ்சாதவனாகவும் இருப்பவனை எதிர்த்து வெல்வது எவருக்கும் கடினமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the invincible nature of a skilled speaker. It identifies three key traits: the ability to speak persuasively ('சொலல் வல்லன்'), the absence of slips or fatigue in speech ('சோர்வு இலன்'), and fearlessness before an audience ('அஞ்சான்'). When a person possesses these three qualities, they become a formidable opponent in any debate or conflict. The word 'இகல்' here refers to a clash of words or ideas, fitting the chapter on the power of speech. Defeating such a person is said to be difficult for anyone.

ai.literal: Swiftly command will obey the world, having arranged sweetly speaking capable people if obtained.
ai.translation: If the world obtains those who can speak with well-arranged thoughts and sweetness, it will swiftly obey their commands.
ai.modern: கருத்துகளை வரிசைப்படுத்தி இனிமையாகச் சொல்லும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களைப் பெற்றால், உலகம் அவர்கள் இடும் கட்டளைகளை விரைந்து ஏற்றுச் செயல்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of organized and pleasant speech. The word 'nirantu' means arranging or ordering, indicating that thoughts must be logically structured before they are spoken. When a person can articulate well-ordered ideas sweetly, the world will not just listen, but will swiftly carry out their commands. The phrase 'tozhil ketkum' specifically implies obeying instructions and taking immediate action.

ai.literal: many things / to say / they will desire / indeed / flaw / without / few things / saying / those who do not know
ai.translation: Those who do not know how to speak a few flawless words will indeed desire to speak at length.
ai.modern: குற்றமில்லாத சில வார்த்தைகளைச் சுருக்கமாகச் சொல்லத் தெரியாதவர்கள், பல வார்த்தைகளை நீட்டிப் பேசவே விரும்புவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the ability to speak concisely with the tendency to talk too much. People who lack the skill to express themselves in a few, flawless words ('மாசு அற்ற சில சொல்லல் தேற்றாதவர்') often try to compensate by saying many things ('பல சொல்லக் காமுறுவர்'). The word 'மன்ற' emphasizes that this is a certain truth. True eloquence lies in clarity and brevity, not in the sheer volume of words.

ai.literal: Even if blossomed in clusters, scentless flowers they are like: what was learned, to understand, having expanded, those who do not speak.
ai.translation: Those who cannot clearly explain what they have learned so that others understand are like flowers that blossom in clusters but yield no fragrance.
ai.modern: தாம் கற்றவற்றை மற்றவர்கள் உணரும்படி விரிவாக எடுத்துச் சொல்ல முடியாதவர்கள், கொத்தாக மலர்ந்திருந்தாலும் மணம் வீசாத மலர்களைப் போன்றவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares learned people who lack the skill of communication to scentless flowers. The phrase 'இண்ருழ்த்தும் நாறா மலர்' (flowers that bloom in clusters but lack fragrance) creates a vivid image of something visually impressive but lacking its essential, appealing quality. Similarly, 'கற்றது உணர விரித்து உரையாதார்' refers to those who have acquired knowledge but cannot expand on it clearly for others to grasp. The comparison emphasizes that knowledge, like a flower's beauty, is unfulfilled if it cannot be effectively shared and appreciated by others.
